newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Gains to VSZ shares push Slovak BSE higher.
newsitem.headline: Gains to VSZ shares push Slovak BSE higher.

text.p: Most major Slovak shares were steady in thin trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, with gains to shares of steel maker VSZ pushing the SAX index up 0.38 points to 179.20.
Brokers said the market's shift to a higher gear after the Christmas holiday was slower that in neighbouring countries, but noted there were signs it would pick up in the near future.
Only three issues traded on the BSE floor on Thursday, with VSZ steel seeing the largest floor volume closing up 10 crowns at 620 with 3,420 shares traded.

"Larger volumes in VSZ and the VUB Kupon investment fund may indicate the usual practise of foreign investors who come first to the most liquid issues and then bring higher trading to other shares," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
VUB Kupon closed up 35 crowns at 650. Oil refiner Slovnaft lost 10 crowns to close at 690.
Overall volume fell to 215,487 shares, consisting mainly of direct trades, from 1,167,631 stocks traded on Wednesday and the turnover was 62.59 million crowns, down from 465.24 million.
